item.title: Bauhaus (font) type-classification?
item.description: I’m organising my font library and am not sure how those super-round typefaces like Bauhaus are classified. “Modern” or “Sans” just isn’t specific enough. Thanks!

item.title: What classification would you give to FS Albert
item.description:
I’m trying to classify FS Albert.

I think it’s a (Neo)-grotesque font, but then it doesn’t have tight apertures and ‘g’ you might expect.

Anybody got any suggestions?

item.title: genre/classifications question
item.description:
what would you classify the typeface used on this site under? http://andren.tumblr.com/
or the headlines on here http://www.dazeddigital.com/

what I really want to do is find more similar typefaces. I would put Officina Serif maybe Courier in the same feel I’m looking for too. I’m at a loss of words to describe it which is why I’m asking if there’s a classification for it.

I’d say it is the kind of sans-serif with serifs/tails for recognition purposes rather than stemming from calligraphic origins. These typefaces are almost very technical in that they’re devoid of any hint of human hand. But not in the way Klavika or Bank Gothic looks techy.

item.title: Typeface Classifications ?
item.description:
Recently I came upon a typeface class called, Realist(you guys have probably heard about it). Is it the same as Grostesque, because I saw it used for typefaces such as Akzidenz and Franklin Gothic. If not, can you please tell me about some of its characteristics.

I basically know(I think) all the general classes but can someone list them and their defining characteristics.

Thanks

item.title: Arabic Classification?
item.description:
